title: Operator Scenario Journal and Prioritization Matrix
author: Aisha Martinez
body:
Summary

This page is the canonical journal and prioritization artifact for platform degradation scenarios used by platform operators, reliability engineers, and SREs. It captures: the scenario definition, measured risk (SLO/latency/cost), a reproducible experiment recipe, operator checklist, and a lightweight prioritization matrix used during quarterly planning and game days.

Why this exists

- Provide a single, searchable place for scenario definitions and outcomes so teams avoid repeating experiments.
- Enable objective prioritization of remediation work by combining likelihood, customer impact, and operator cost.
- Speed up onboarding for new operators with lab-ready, reproducible recipes and safety gates.

Scope and audience

- Audience: platform operators, eng-platform, eng-sre, runtime, oncall.
- Scope: multi-tenant inference degradation scenarios (latency, KV-prefix cache failures, model-variant fallback storms, tenant burst tokens). Not intended for security or customer PII incidents.

Ownership

- Scenario author: Aisha Martinez (eng-platform/operator-labs)
- Primary owner for triage/remediation: Platform Reliability (eng-sre)
- Escalation: Runtime team (eng-serving-runtime)

How to read this page

- Each numbered scenario below has: summary, measurable SLO impacts, reproducible recipe, operator playbook, recorded outcomes, and follow-up actions.
- Use the Prioritization Matrix (section below) to score new scenarios.

Prioritization matrix (quick reference)

Columns: Scenario ID | Impact bucket (customer-facing) | Likelihood (1–5) | Operator effort (1–5) | Cost delta (1–5) | SLO hit risk (1–5) | Priority (Low/Medium/High)

Example table:

| ID  | Impact        | Likelihood | Op Effort | Cost Delta | SLO Risk | Priority |
|-----|---------------|------------|-----------|------------|----------|----------|
| S-101 | Tail latency spike on small requests | 4 | 3 | 2 | 4 | High |
| S-118 | KV prefix cache shard loss (partial) | 3 | 4 | 3 | 5 | High |
| S-210 | Model-variant fallback storms | 2 | 4 | 4 | 3 | Medium |

Scoring guidance

- Likelihood: historical frequency or probability from operator telemetry.
- Operator effort: estimated hours for detection->mitigation by a single operator.
- Cost delta: expected incremental infra cost while mitigations run (per-hour scale).
- SLO risk: how many customers/SLOs are expected to be impacted (token-level latency, p50/p95/p99).
- Priority computed as: if SLO Risk >=4 and Likelihood >=3 -> High; else if SLO Risk >=3 -> Medium; otherwise Low.

Scenario entries (select examples)

1) S-118 — KV-prefix cache shard loss (partial)

Summary
- A shard of prefix KV cache becomes unreadable (corrupt snapshot, node OOM) causing increased cold-start token cost and tail-latency for affected tenants.

Measurable impact
- p95 token generation latency increases by 40–120ms for requests hitting the missing shard.
- Cache hit ratio drops from 92% to 58% for affected cohorts.
- Cost increase: +18% per-minute token compute for impacted tenants until warmset repopulated.

Reproducible recipe (lab)
1. Deploy synthetic tenant cohort (tenant-sim:kv-shard-118) using the operator-lab CLI.
2. Toggle the lab failure flag: labctl induce kv-shard-failure --shard-id=7 --duration=10m
3. Generate steady-state traffic with workload profile small-chat-high-ttl.yaml (p50=40ms, p99 target 300ms).
4. Observe telemetry in dashboard: /dashboards/kv-cache/shard-health and token-cost-synth.

Operator runbook (immediate actions)
1. Acknowledge page in PagerDuty; add incident tag S-118.
2. Run: opsctl prefetchtask rebuild-shard --shard 7 --priority=high.
3. If rebuild fails after 3 attempts, failover shard: opsctl kv failover --shard 7 --target=shard-13.
4. Monitor p95/p99 and cache hit ratio. If p99 does not return to baseline within 15m, open escalation to runtime (tag @runtime).

Observed outcomes (lab run 2025-12-07)
- Rebuild completed in 7 minutes; p95 recovered to baseline in 12 minutes.
- Operator effort: 0.6h. Follow-up action: add a preflight check that detects >30% drop in hit ratio and auto-schedule rebuild.

2) S-101 — Tail latency spike on small requests

Summary
- Small, low-token requests see increased p99 during batch consolidation windows on specific GPU types when background quantization kernels are scheduled.

Measurable impact
- p50 unchanged; p99 increases from 210ms -> 420ms across regional pool eu-west-1b.
- Affects ~4% of traffic but causes customer-facing latency alerts.

Recipe
- labctl schedule kernel-switch --pool=eu-west-1b --window=30m --kernel=quant-opt-3
- Generate 2000 small requests/min using traffic-generator small-requests.yaml

Immediate mitigations
1. Admin: set pool kernel to conservative path: opsctl pool set-kernel --pool eu-west-1b --kernel=latency-safe
2. If unresolved, divert small requests to warmset-enabled pool: opsctl traffic steer --filter small-requests --target warmset-pool

Retrospective notes (2026-01-09)
- Root cause: automatic aggressive kernel scheduling during off-peak that did not account for small-request bursts.
- Remediation: change scheduling policy to require warmset score >=0.6 before aggressive kernels applied.

Operator checklist (common tasks for any scenario)

- Detection
  - Confirm alert source and correlated traces (token-cost, latency, model-fallback).
  - Identify affected cohort: tenant ids, regions, pools.
- Mitigation
  - Apply targeted failover or kernel downgrade using opsctl.
  - Enable synthetic fallback if model outputs are timing-sensitive.
- Recovery
  - Validate SLI return to baseline for 30m before closing.
  - Document operator actions in incident timeline.
- Post-incident
  - Create follow-up ticket with suggested owner and estimated effort.
  - If cost delta >5% sustained, schedule remediation for the next sprint.

Experiment template (copyable)

--- experiment: S-XXX-template
description: Short one-line description
injection: labctl induce <failure-mode> --params
traffic_profile: /lab/profiles/<profile>.yaml
metrics: [p50_latency, p95_latency, cache_hit_ratio, token_cost_delta]
run_duration: 20m
rollback: labctl rollback <failure-id>
---

Safety and gating

- Never run scenarios tagged "production-safety" without a cross-team sign-off.
- For any experiment that injects real capacity evictions, set a hard stop at 10% global capacity impact. Use opsctl safe-stop --max-capacity-impact=10.

Quarterly roadmap actions (derived from journal)

- Q1 2026: Implement auto-detect and auto-schedule rebuild for KV-shard drop (owner: eng-infra).
- Q2 2026: Kernel scheduling policy change — add warmset gating and operator override (owner: runtime).
- Q3 2026: Build operator training lab with scenario playback UI and one-click replay (owner: platform-operator-experience).

Retrospective capture format (use for every closed scenario)

- Title: short descriptive title
- Incident ID: internal id (S-XXX)
- Date ran/occurred
- Time to detect / Time to mitigate / Time to recover
- Operator actions (bulleted)
- Root cause summary (1–2 sentences)
- Follow-ups (owner + due date)

Appendix: dashboards and queries (links & snippets)

- Key dashboards:
  - KV shard health: /dashboards/kv-cache/shard-health
  - Token cost synth: /dashboards/cost/token-synth
  - Tail latency investigator: /dashboards/latency/tail-investigator

- Example PromQL snippet to detect shard loss:
  - sum(rate(kv_cache_gets_total{shard!~""}[1m])) by (shard) / ignoring(shard) group_left sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total{shard!~""}[1m])) by (shard) < 0.6

How to contribute a new scenario

1. Fork this page (create a new entry below this document with a new S-XXX id).
2. Add metadata: author, date, expected impact, reproducible recipe, and telemetry links.
3. Run the experiment in the lab first; record outcomes.
4. Submit for review with the label "scenario-review" and add at least two reviewers.

Appendix B: Glossary

- Warmset: the runtime construct that keeps KV-prefix state resident to reduce cold starts.
- Prefetch/rebuild: operator-initiated background job to repopulate KV shards.

Contact and escalation

- For immediate operational escalation: #platform-ops (Slack) and PagerDuty: Platform-Ops
- For runtime or kernel issues: @runtime on-call
